answer: A bio-photonic attestation protocol binds agent identities to chlorophyll fluorescence within an agricultural oasis. To authenticate, an agent streams photochemical decay kinetics from a live saffron bed or climbing vine under pulsed light excitation. An attacker must provision dedicated fluorometer hardware and organic tissue per identity, incurring linear capital costs. However, photoinhibition or thermal stress can alter fluorescence yields, spuriously rejecting valid agents.
